subject: Service economics & health: April dashboard deep-sync + QBR actions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com>, Sanjeev Reddy <sanjeev@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service economics & health: April dashboard deep-sync + QBR actions

Team — attaching the April KPI snapshot for the service surface (latency, cost per 1k tokens, uptime, monthly active routes). I pulled this ahead of next week's QBR prep so we can lock owners on the key asks. High-level notes: 

- Usage: +22% MoM overall, driven by two new partner integrations (Acme test and FastCloud pilot).
- Latency: p50 stable, p95 shows a ~120ms uplift on long-context routes (>=1024 tokens) starting 3/20.
- Cost: effective per-token cost up ~6% due to more long-context calls and fewer cache hits.
- Uptime: 99.94% this window; we saw a 15-minute blip on 3/28 tied to a node restart in us-west-2.

Requests: 
1) Vivek — can you confirm whether the p95 increase is from scheduling/batching changes or model variant routing? Please give a short root-cause hypothesis + corrective runbook by EOD Monday.
2) Marcus — please attach the ops tickets for the 3/28 restart and an ETA for the preventative fix (single-node hardening).
3) Grace — for the QBR slide deck, can you pull a 90-day trend for cost per 1k tokens and a short note on the Acme pilot contribution?

Attachments: 2027-04_dashboard_apr.pdf (dashboard, 12 pages)

Thanks — I want this consolidated before the leadership dry-run.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com>, Sanjeev Reddy <sanjeev@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service economics & health: April dashboard deep-sync + QBR actions

Thanks Rachel — quick read and a few notes: 

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 09:12 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the April KPI snapshot for the service surface (...)

Preliminary take: the p95 drift looks correlated with a change in route-matching that sent a small subset (~2.3% of requests) to the long-context optimized runtime with a different batching profile. Our telemetry shows those requests now batch at slightly larger window sizes (to amortize warm-start cost), which increases tail latency when traffic bursts hit.

Action plan (owner: Vivek):
- Short-term (next 48h): revert the routing rule for the flagged route-group to previous variant (low-risk config flip). I can do this and monitor; expected p95 improvement within one hour of flip.
- Medium (2 weeks): adjust the batch window heuristic to be queue-length aware and add an A/B to validate tail behavior.
- Long (quarter): kernel-level latency budget enforcement for long-context paths + more aggressive KV cache warming.

I'll open a CI rollback PR now and include the test-run artifacts. Marcus — I'll coordinate with you on the flip window so ops can be on-call.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service economics & health: April dashboard deep-sync + QBR actions

Good notes — I pulled the ops artifacts for the 3/28 incident and created a short ticket chain.

Incident summary (ticket RG-4521):
- 3/28 02:17 UTC: scheduled node reboot (non-disruptive) hit a timing edge with a GC pause on a hot process; that caused a delayed swarm restart and a 15-minute reduction in capacity in us-west-2.
- Mitigation taken: emergency scale-up + traffic spill to us-east-1; customer-facing impact minimal but recorded.

Follow-ups (owner: Marcus):
- RG-4522: add pre-reboot health-check gating to prevent restart during GC windows. ETA: 4/11.
- RG-4523: hardening to ensure faster container restart (tuned graceful shutdown). ETA: 4/18.
- RG-4524: postmortem doc + customer note (we'll draft a short message for Acme).

Attachments: uptime_log_excerpt.csv (excerpt of node logs)

I'll stand by for Vivek's routing flip so we can coordinate the window and update the postmortem.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Manager, Production Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Sanjeev Reddy <sanjeev@acme.com>, Lina Harper <lina.harper@fastcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service economics & health: April dashboard deep-sync + QBR actions

Thanks — consolidated update for the QBR pack and next steps below.

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 10:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com> wrote:
> Good notes — I pulled the ops artifacts for the 3/28 incident and created a short ticket chain.

QBR slide asks (what I'll prepare by Tues EOD):
- A one-slide summary: 90-day trend for cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, uptime % (highlighting the 3/28 blip).
- A short narrative (3 bullets) on root causes and mitigations we own (routing flip, ops hardening, batching heuristic work).
- Acme pilot contribution: callouts on usage lift (+22% MoM) and projected ARR if we move from pilot to standard integration (I have a revenue estimate + sensitivity table).

Meeting scheduling: can we do a 30-min dry-run Wed 04/07 10:00–10:30 PT? I want to walk the slide, the fallback policy (what to say if latency/regression questions come up), and confirm owners for the follow-up action list.

Open questions for leadership call: 
- Do we want to propose a short-term cache-warming credit for Acme while we roll the routing flip?
- Approval to accelerate RG-4523 (hardening) to high priority if we see any repeat blips.

If everyone is good, I'll assemble the single-page QBR slide and a two-item exec note (what happened, what we did, next 30d).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product, Platform
Redwood Inference
